A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. assessment.reason: There is a large model/market gap on a projected mean just above the 1.5 line. The gap hinges on a modest 16.6-minute projection, so Zacha's actual deployment could swing the direction.
assessment.model_case: Projected mean of about 1.56 shots with median one. The under is favored only through distribution skew. The shrunk shot rate and modest ice time do the work. A heavier role would push the mean toward two and flip the case.
assessment.price_case: Main 1.5 line at +132 needs roughly +132 break-even. Model fair is about -120 and the minimum is about +105, but the market implies the over is favored. A gap this wide suggests books project more volume.

findings.note: Novak's NHL.com profile lists 130 shots in 82 games in 2025-26, about 1.6 per game, and his playoff game log shows 1 shot or fewer in 4 of his last 5 games. This is past data only, and no current game-day injury or lineup status turned up.

A Rotowire note from July 31, 2026 says Novak is expected to move into the second-line center role for 2026-27, which could mean more ice time and more shots. It also says Ben Kindel is pushing for a top-six spot and that Novak struggled late last season.

On Oct. 4, 2026, Novak scored twice against Montreal, including an overtime winner set up by Malkin. That suggests he may be playing alongside Malkin, but the clip has no shot totals and it's unclear whether that game was preseason.
In the Oct. 20 loss at St. Louis, Perfetti scored his sixth goal in nine games. That keeps him at about a point per game, but the Jets have lost three straight and scored only once in that game.

Before training camp, Perfetti was moved up to the top line with Connor and Scheifele. He had 8 points in his first 8 games, tied for second on the team, and the article says he is healthy after last season's ankle injury.

The Jets' projected lineup for Oct. 20 had Perfetti on the first line with Kyle Connor and Mark Scheifele. That points to steady top-six minutes going into the Dallas game. No injury news for him turned up.

In a game a week before this one (Oct 15, 2026), Hughes scored twice in a 7-1 win over the Rangers, his first NHL multigoal game, and coach Keefe said he has been really good all season. That points to a healthy, productive player, which works against the Under.

This is older (Nov 2025). It says Hughes led the Devils with nearly 23 minutes a night and played on both the power play and the penalty kill. Heavy use like that gives him more chances to get a point, though it is not current proof of how he is being used now.

He went on long-term injured reserve in Jan 2026 with a shoulder injury, his second shoulder injury after surgery in 2025. He had 26 points in 49 games before it, a rate that often means no point in a game. I found no current injury news, lineup news or picks for this Oct 22 game.

NHL.com (2 days ago): Stenberg has 15 shots on goal in 10 games, which is exactly 1.5 per game and matches the line. He plays mostly middle-six minutes with Misa and Sherwood, and gets about 3:10 per game on the top power-play unit with Celebrini and Smith.

CBS/RotoWire (Oct 18): In the Oct 17 game at Detroit, Stenberg had 3 shots in 17:30 of ice time, including 7:53 on the power play. The piece says his usage is growing and he has two multi-point games in his last three outings, which points to shot volume that could go over 1.5.
NHL.com (Sept 23, preseason only): In his preseason debut against Vegas, Stenberg had 4 shots on goal in 22:17 of ice time. That shows he can put up shot volume when he gets heavy minutes.
